summary: Afternoon surge: sustained 5xx wave after customer enabled high-throughput streaming (proxy connection leak + prefetch spill)
description: Issue summary: LuminaHealth began reporting elevated 5xx rates (503/502) and streaming resets starting ~2026-03-11 14:10 PDT after enabling a high-throughput streaming integration. Impact: Several service endpoints returned sustained 5xx for ~90 minutes, degrading real-time app behavior and triggering customer alerts. Environment: prod-us-west dedicated tenant on Redwood Dedicated. Immediate customer impact: realtime chat sessions dropping, message retries, increased latency.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer set client concurrency to 200 simultaneous streaming sessions (per-tenant).
Client uses keepalive-enabled HTTP/2 connections with aggressive prefetch headers (X-Redwood-Prefetch: true).
Start sustained high QPS (10k RPS sustained across sessions) from a small set of client IPs.
Observe API gateway 502/503 rates and runtime restarts in tenant logs.
logs: runtime-stdout: 2026-03-11T14:13:02Z runtime exited signal: SIGKILL (OOM) pid=23491 tenant=lumina-01 memory=172GB
investigation_notes: 14:20 - Support confirmed error spike coincides with customer's concurrency change via audit logs (customer claims change pushed at 14:05).
14:34 - Observed long-lived connections from 3 client IPs holding >100 streams each; keepalive pool exhaustion on apigw nodes (connection reuse failing).
14:45 - Runtime showed progressive memory pressure on tenant's serving instances; OOMs correlated with large prefetch queue growth (prefetch configured at client-side + server-side prefetch enabled).

15:00 - Autoscaler responded with rapid scale-up/down cycles (thrashing) because new replicas were cold and prefetch backlog persisted; this amplified connection churn and caused additional 502s from unhealthy upstreams.

15:30 - Hypothesis: combination of aggressive client prefetch + insufficient connection pool limits + autoscaler cooldown too aggressive => cascading retries, runtime memory pressure, and OOM-triggered exits.
comments: 2026-03-11 14:25 - Maria Alvarez (Support): Acknowledged to customer and requested traffic samples and exact client config. Suggested temporary throttle to 50 concurrent streams.
2026-03-11 14:40 - LuminaHealth (Customer): Confirmed they rolled out a config change to increase concurrency; can't rollback immediately, asked for immediate mitigation on our side.

2026-03-11 15:05 - Ethan Park (SRE): Temporarily reduced apigw keepalive_pool_size to 64 for tenant lumina-01 and reduced per-tenant prefetch window. Observed 40% drop in upstream OOMs within 10 minutes.
2026-03-11 16:10 - Priya Desai (Platform Eng): Pushed new autoscaler cooldown tweak to avoid aggressive scale down for 10m for the affected pool (canary). Monitoring for stability.
2026-03-12 09:14 - Customer Success (Jared Nguyen): Customer accepted temporary throttle; requested timeline for root-cause fix and postmortem.
resolution: Workaround applied: temporarily limited per-tenant streaming concurrency to 50 and disabled server-side prefetch for lumina-01. Autoscaler cooldown increased to prevent thrash. Permanent fix in progress: PR #2783 updates proxy connection-pool bookkeeping to avoid connection leak under heavy stream fanout and adds backpressure on prefetch queue; target rollout to prod-us-west on 2026-03-15 after canary verification. Customer notified and agreed to staged rollout. Follow-up: create monitoring alert for prefetch_queue_len > 5000 and add automated tenant throttling policy if sustained > 5m.
